messages:
sam: pushed the new 'Granular Chargeback' dashboard prototype to staging: https://staging.redwood/costs/chargeback :eyes:

jia: saw it — nice. quick q: the 'cache savings' column, is that being double-counted? i.e. saved tokens subtracted at route level and again at model level?

sam: good catch. current prototype subtracts cache hits from the route totals and also shows model-level savings separately (so it's shown twice but labelled). that's confusing.

mike: i vote we show both gross and net columns. Gross = raw tokens, Net = gross - apportioned_cache_savings. And then a separate breakdown panel that shows how savings are apportioned (model vs route vs consumer).

katie: important: chargeback for internal teams should reflect cache savings so teams don't game by disabling shared cache. we need a policy that can be enforced when exporting monthly chargebacks.

jia: suggest an "apportionment" model. options: 1) attribute all cache savings to the model serving the response, 2) attribute to the route that triggered the request, 3) weighted share based on token origin metadata. add a knob in the UI to pick.

mike: agree. UX: default to 'model' for simplicity, but have a tooltip: "Why model? -> cache tied to model artifacts; choose route to prioritize product-level ownership."

sam: implementation detail — we must avoid exploding cardinality in the dashboard queries. If apportionment is weighted by consumer or route, that's high-card. propose pre-aggregations + daily materialized table for savings attribution.

cost-bot: nightly job scheduled: refresh_mv_chargeback_savings at 03:10 UTC. last run: success. duration: 2m12s.

jia: proto SQL for apportioned savings (very rough):

```
WITH hits AS (
  SELECT route, model, sum(hit_tokens) as hit_tokens
  FROM cache_events
  WHERE ts >= current_date - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY route, model
), total_hits AS (
  SELECT sum(hit_tokens) as total FROM hits
)
SELECT
  route,
  model,
  hit_tokens,
  (hit_tokens::float / total) * global_cache_cost as apportioned_savings
FROM hits, total_hits;
```

jia: that example uses global_cache_cost as the nightly compute-backed number (cost of cache ops). we can expose that as a config.

katie: for chargeback export we need: route_id, model_id, gross_tokens, net_tokens, cache_savings_apportioned, unit_cost. and a versioned schema so finance can reconcile.

mike: UX asks: surface 7d/30d rolling windows, and add a per-rollout toggle so product can see canary vs prod splits. also an API param so infra can fetch machine-readable numbers for automation.

sam: agreed. i'll add a backend flag: cache_attribution_policy with values ["model","route","weighted"], and a new endpoint /v1/internal/chargeback_summary?window=30d&apportion=weighted

katie: minor but important: tooltip language needs to explain that 'weighted' is approximate and may not map 1:1 to billing invoices. keep billing docs separate. i'll draft.

cost-bot: note: exposing per-request token-level unit cost increases query cost. recommend materialized daily aggregates and an API for high-card queries.

jia: ok i will: 1) update the aggregations to emit apportioned_savings per (route,model,day), 2) add a nightly job to compute 7/30d rolling pre-aggregates.

sam: i'll wire the new API field and add the UI toggle in staging. i'll also add a flag to hide high-card views behind a permission (product/finance).

mike: i'll mock the tooltip copy + add the 7/30d toggle in the dashboard.

katie: i'll draft the chargeback export schema and loop in finance.

sam: follow-up: sync tomorrow 10am PT to finalize assumptions. if anyone needs to change the apportionment defaults before then, ping here. :thumbsup:
